findings.text: The gauges shared {{metric:common_minutes}} of valid daily records. The requested window contained {{metric:outside_common_minutes}} outside that common time.

Integrating the reported daily means gave {{metric:left_L}} at the Potomac gauge and {{metric:right_L}} at the Northwest Branch Anacostia gauge. The signed difference, Potomac minus Northwest Branch, was +{{metric:difference_L}}.

Under the editor’s rate-error scenario, the minimum signed difference was +{{metric:difference_low_L}} with Potomac at its lower bound and Northwest Branch at its upper bound. Reversing the extremes gave a maximum of +{{metric:difference_high_L}}. The positive minimum supports the Potomac’s larger integrated volume throughout the stated scenario.

The Daily-record auditor identified three matching local dates in the USGS daily discharge series (parameter 00060, mean statistic 00003). I verified an A qualifier on all six values. USGS defines A as completed processing and review for publication. April 3 contributed its full daily mean, so the common window ran from midnight April 1, 2023 up to midnight April 4 EDT, with three 86,400-second days. The auditor confirmed the dates, conversion and native-unit arithmetic in shared entries gxtmsg_01m8fr8vjvsc5f845x and gxtmsg_01m8frarhax1j5rkkq.

In date order, the original Potomac rates at Little Falls (01646500) were 9,980, 9,230 and 8,630 ft³/s. Northwest Branch near Hyattsville (01651000) had 60.9, 40.7 and 25.9 ft³/s. Multiplying each station’s sum by 86,400 s gives 2,405,376,000 ft³ and 11,016,000 ft³, respectively, for a signed difference of +2,394,360,000 ft³. All six prepared rates match the source rates using 1 ft³ = 28.316846592 L, and the volumes agree with paired.json.

Each prepared absolute rate bound equals 25% of its approved daily mean. With P and N denoting nominal Potomac and Northwest Branch volumes, the native-unit bounds are 0.75P − 1.25N = +1,790,262,000 ft³ and 1.25P − 0.75N = +2,998,458,000 ft³. These are deterministic limits under the editor’s assumption that each daily rate can range independently within its bound. The approval qualifier describes USGS review status.
